title: ARISE Insect DNA Extraction
author: Kevin Beentjes
materials: Tissue Sampling Note: For high throughput, DNA extraction can be performed in plates rather than individual tubes. Within ARISE animal tissues are processed in Nunc 96-wells plates (Avantor cat no. 732-2661), which are used for photography, tissue lysis and sample storage. Add 50 μl of Lysis Buffer A into a plate or 1.5 ml eppendorf tube. Place up to 40 mg of tissue (e.g. a single insect leg) into the plate / tube, small insects can be added to the buffer in their entirety for a non-destructive DNA extraction. This is at your own risk! Only applicable for hard-bodied insects, there is no guarantee that specimens are not damaged or destroyed during lysis. Optional: Grind tissue with a tube pestle or cut the tissue with a scalpel. For non-destructive DNA extractions, skip this step. Possible stop, store samples at 4 °C. At this step, photography of specimens is possible without the risk of buffers crystallizing (since Lysis Buffer B has not been added yet).

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer A
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL Lysis Buffer A by mixing Tris‑HCl, EDTA and water, adjusting pH, and bringing to final volume.

substeps.instruction: Add 13.4 mL of 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8) to 50 mL Milli‑Q water.
Add 10.6 mL of 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8) and stir until all solids dissolve.
Adjust the solution to pH 9.0 with NaOH.
Bring the final volume to 100 mL with Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer B
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL Lysis Buffer B, dissolve salts, adjust pH, and bring to final volume; heat if salts crystallize.

substeps.instruction: Add 3.4 g guanidine thiocyanate, 17.4 g trisodium phosphate dodecahydrate, and 0.4 g NaCl to 50 mL Milli‑Q water.
Stir on a heated magnetic stirrer until all solids are dissolved.
If salts crystallize, heat at ~55 °C for 10 min until dissolved.
Adjust the solution to pH 9.0 with 5 M HCl.
Bring the final volume to 100 mL with Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Lysis Additive
steps.instruction: Make a 15 % Tween‑20 solution for tissue lysis.

substeps.instruction: Add 15 mL Tween‑20 to 85 mL Milli‑Q water.
Stir gently, avoiding bubble formation.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Binding Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 mL Tissue Binding Buffer containing guanidine hydrochloride and ethanol; heat if needed.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 26.3 g guanidine hydrochloride in 20 mL Milli‑Q water and stir until clear.
Adjust the volume to 50 mL with Milli‑Q water.
Add 50 mL 100 % ethanol.
If salts crystallize, heat at ~55 °C for 10 min until dissolved.

steps.title: Prepare Elution Buffer
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL Elution Buffer for DNA recovery.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8) to 75 mL Milli‑Q water.
Add 0.2 mL 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8).
Bring the final volume to 100 mL with Milli‑Q water.
Vortex or stir briefly to mix.

steps.title: Make Lysis Mixture & Calibration Solution
steps.instruction: Combine buffers to create a lysis mixture, then prepare a calibration solution to set the correct pH for the Tissue Binding Buffer.

substeps.instruction: Mix 2.17 mL Lysis Buffer A, 2.17 mL Lysis Buffer B, 330 µL Milli‑Q, and 330 µL 15 % Tween‑20 to obtain the lysis mixture.
In a 50 mL tube add 10 mL Tissue Binding Buffer to 5 mL of the lysis mixture.
Adjust the pH to 4.0–4.5 with 5 M HCl (approximately 350 µL; record the exact volume added).
Keep the mixture at room temperature and mix thoroughly.
Dispose of this calibration solution.

steps.title: Verify & Adjust Binding Buffer pH
steps.instruction: Use the recorded HCl volume to set the pH of all Tissue Binding Buffer batches and verify the pH.

substeps.instruction: For each 10 mL of Tissue Binding Buffer to be used, add the same volume of 5 M HCl recorded from the calibration step (e.g., 350 µL per 10 mL; 3.5 mL for 100 mL).
Verify pH by mixing 10 mL binding buffer with 5 mL fresh lysis mixture and measuring; adjust as needed to stay between pH 4.0 and 4.5.

steps.title: Bind DNA to Magnetic Beads
steps.instruction: Pellet solids, transfer lysate, add magnetic beads and binding buffer, then incubate.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge incubated samples at maximum speed, room temperature for 1 min to pellet solid particles.
Transfer 75 µL supernatant to a deep‑well plate or tube.
Add 20 µL SeraSil‑Mag 400 beads (ensure beads are fully resuspended).
Add 150 µL Tissue Binding Buffer (2 × the lysate volume).
Incubate 5 min at room temperature on a shaker.

steps.title: Chemical Lysis with Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add additional buffers and Proteinase K to each sample and incubate for thorough lysis.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL Lysis Buffer B, 7.7 µL Tissue Lysis Additive, and 7.7 µL Proteinase K solution (36 mg/mL) per sample.
Incubate at 55 °C, 400 RPM on a shaking incubator (or vortex intermittently) for at least 3 hours or overnight.
If needed, store samples at 4 °C after incubation.

steps.title: Wash Magnetic Beads
steps.instruction: Perform sequential washes to remove contaminants from the bead‑bound DNA.

substeps.instruction: Place plate/tube on a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Remove from magnet, add 500 µL isopropanol, shake at room temperature 500 RPM for 2 min.
Settle beads on magnet and discard supernatant.
Add 400 µL 96 % ethanol, shake, settle, and discard supernatant.
Repeat the 400 µL ethanol wash once more (total two ethanol washes).
Remove all residual ethanol and dry beads for 5–10 min at room temperature (or 50 °C).

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Release DNA from beads into elution buffer and collect the purified solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 50–70 µL Elution Buffer (or Milli‑Q) to each sample.
Shake at 500 RPM for at least 5 min.
Settle beads on the magnet and transfer the supernatant to a new plate or tube.
